title: Logic and critical reasoning
audience: a high-school student (grades 9–12) or an adult reviewing high-school work
purpose: Analyze and evaluate arguments rigorously: standard form and argument diagrams, deductive validity and soundness, categorical logic with Venn diagrams, propositional logic with truth tables, informal fallacies, inductive and statistical reasoning, causal reasoning with Mill's methods, arguments from analogy and inference to the best explanation.
primary_reading: Introduction to Logic and Critical Thinking (Open Textbook Library, free)

weeks.2: Deduction and induction: validity, soundness and strength
weeks.3: Categorical statements and the square of opposition
weeks.6: Truth tables for statements: tautologies, contradictions and contingencies
weeks.7: Truth tables for arguments: testing validity
weeks.8: Short truth tables and common valid forms
weeks.12: Analogy and inference to the best explanation

blocks.deliverable: Put eight passages in standard form and diagram two.
Test ten syllogisms with Venn diagrams.
Translate ten English sentences into symbols.
Week 7 midterm; test five arguments with truth tables.
Identify the fallacies in a sample letter to the editor.
Evaluate a causal claim from a news report.
Submit the project; take an unseen 60 minute final in week 14.

project: Logic casebook: choose four arguments from public sources (an opinion column, a court opinion, a classic philosophical text and a scientific claim), put each in standard form, test the deductive ones with truth tables or Venn diagrams, evaluate the inductive ones for strength, name every fallacy, and write a one-page verdict on each.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
